headline: FirstQFM, a Stockholm company, said it is one of four groups chosen to test D-Wave's error-detecting quantum computer design in a software simulator.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 2: this repeats the D-Wave beta program we carried on 7 Oct; the only new item is FirstQFM's statement of its own role.
importance_line: Researchers and a bank get to practise error-aware quantum programming before D-Wave's machine exists, but the 90% error-detection figure is D-Wave's own claim, the hardware is not built, and the program itself is not new.
summary: FirstQFM, a company that builds AI foundation models for quantum computing, says in a release that it joins BBVA, Florida Atlantic University and Germany's Jülich Supercomputing Centre in D-Wave's beta program, which gives early access to a simulator of D-Wave's planned gate-model quantum computer, and that it will use the simulator to test how detected errors can improve results. D-Wave says its dual-rail design is built to detect about 90% of errors, a company claim; the program began at the start of October and we carried it in our 7 Oct 2026 edition, so little here is new.
notes: Quantum Zeitgeist (10 Oct) rewrote FirstQFM's release, so the release is credited and linked; both read. Beta program launch dated 1 Oct 2026 from Google News listings of D-Wave's release copies (not read); our 7 Oct edition carried it as C15-11. Category MOD (product/tool) as for the 7 Oct entry, from default RES.
